facts.fact: Benin's playbook for ID4Africa 2026 states that under law 2020-34 of 6 January 2021 paper civil-status registers are abolished and civil status is dematerialised, that every birth is now registered in the RNPP, which counts as its declaration to the civil status and gives the child the NPI, and that at death the person's status is updated automatically in the RNPP; it lists keeping data current through death registration among its challenges. The deck gives no date for the practice, so its publication month is used.
facts.system: Fichier National de l'État Civil (FNEC), interoperable with the RNPP

facts.fact: The playbook states that ANIP, attached to the Presidency, carries the identity and civil-status reform and is in charge of the population register, the national civil-status file and the electoral file, its director general being a civil-status officer with national competence; the Interior ministry's civil-status directorate keeps the national civil-status policy. No date is given, so the publication month is used.
facts.system: Fichier National de l'État Civil (FNEC), interoperable with the RNPP

facts.fact: The playbook states that Benin chose a sovereign approach, self-financing the initial RAVIP and the setting up of the RNPP, and that revenue from identity cards, certificates and civil-status acts (birth, death, marriage) goes into ANIP's resources, with the World Bank's WURI project and UNICEF also contributing; it says the economic model is still being drawn up, for presentation in 2027, and names no budget line. No date is given, so the publication month is used.
facts.system: Fichier National de l'État Civil (FNEC), interoperable with the RNPP
